co_winterfest_wall.blurb: Winterfest Wall is a compact stretch of the North Table Mountain cliff band above Golden, formed from dark volcanic lava flows. Most routes are bolted and short, a little over half a rope length, so laps go quickly; a good share of the lines are trad. The grades centre on 5.10 and 5.11, with a few easier 5.8 and 5.9 lines below and several 5.12s above. Sunset Arete, Silver Bullet and Crawling Up Roseanne's Belly are favorites. The wall looks west and takes sun through the afternoon, so it is pleasant on cold days and warm in summer. Expect loose rock near the tops and plenty of company on weekends.

co_bastille_n_face_the.blurb: The north side of the Bastille is a steep wall of about 350 feet in Eldorado Canyon, reached straight from the road after a short uphill walk from the car and a bridge over the creek. It is almost all trad, with crack systems, many variations and sustained, exposed climbing. Most lines sit at 5.10 and 5.11, with a few moderates, so it suits intermediate and strong leaders rather than beginners. The Bastille Crack (5.7) is the best-known moderate; Werk Supp, Outer Space and Wide Country are other classics. The face stays shaded for most of the day, cool in summer but cold and windy in shoulder seasons. Expect loose rock, aging fixed gear, a walk-off descent and busy weekends.

co_bihedral_upper_tier_the.blurb: The Upper Tier of the Bihedral is a granite crag in Boulder Canyon, marked by a big left-facing dihedral split partway up by a prow. The rock is hard grey granite, a bit less than vertical, with good friction and a mix of slopers and incut edges. Trad and bolted lines run from about 5.7 to 5.12, with the weight at 5.8 through 5.10, which makes it a favorite for groups and newer leaders. Bihedral Arete (5.10a) is the classic, with Thumb Tack and Sands of Iwo Jima (both 5.11d) for harder climbers. The crag gets sun and is often sheltered from wind, so it suits warm, still winter days. Watch for loose rock above; the usual way down is a rappel into a gully.

co_turtle_rocks_camping_area.blurb: Turtle Rocks is a bouldering area just north of Buena Vista, built around a group of rounded formations beside a campground. The stone has coarse, large crystals, and some faces, especially the overhung ones on South Turtle Rock, are sharp enough to be hard on skin, so tape up. The Sunshine Wall on the south side of Turtle Rock is the social center, a slightly overhung corridor with room to hang out and views. Problems run from V0 to V8, mostly V1 through V5 with a solid group at V4 to V6. Instant Karma (V5), Angel Fire (V6) and Vaguely Dog-like Creature (V4-5) are standouts.

co_neanderthal_wall.blurb: Neanderthal Wall is a short, steep cliff on the west rim of Castlewood Canyon, a small canyon cut by Cherry Creek southeast of Denver. Routes are brief, roughly 50 to 60 feet, and mix trad, top-rope and bolted lines. Grades spread widely but cluster between 5.7 and 5.11, with a few harder tests such as Stratego (5.12a, top rope) and Unshackled Minds (5.13b). The Mosh (5.8) and Outer Mongolia (5.10) are good places to start. Rock quality varies, with sandy cracks and some old quarter-inch bolts, so back up single bolts and bring a trad rack. The approach from the south parking area is a moderate walk on dusty trail with some elevation gain.

co_vestibule_the.blurb: The Vestibule is a corridor running between the main towers of the Monastery, high above Big Thompson Canyon near Estes Park. The climbing is nearly all sport, on finer-grained rock than much of the Monastery with crisp edges and holds, steep slabs on one side and vertical to overhanging walls on the other. Grades start around 5.9 and reach 5.14, with the bulk between 5.11 and 5.13. Tabula Rasa, Stolen Land, Psychatomic, The Quickening and Grand Ol' Opry draw strong climbers. Allow most of an hour for the hike, which drops steeply first and makes for a hard walk out. The crags are high enough to be cold on cloudy days, and rattlesnakes live in the area.

co_wall_of_the_90s.blurb: Wall of the '90s is a sport wall on the south side of US 6 in Clear Creek Canyon, just west of Tunnel 2 outside Golden. Climbing is on solid canyon gneiss, with the walls taking afternoon and evening sun. It is a destination for hard sport climbing: more than half the routes are 5.12 or harder, up to 5.14, with a middle band of 5.10s and 5.11s that includes Curvaceous (5.11b), Wet Dream (5.12a) and Ten-Digit Dialing (5.12c). Hellcat and Mission Impossible are among the hardest. Some routes are long, so knot the rope ends. The approach is short, steep and a little slippery, with scree overhead.

co_ouray_rotary_park_rink_wall.blurb: The Rink Wall is a short sport cliff in Rotary Park at the north edge of Ouray, with restrooms, a picnic area under cottonwoods and a few steps between the car and the base. The main wall is slabby, with short, well-protected single-pitch leads; steeper and harder lines lie around the corner to the right and stay fairly dry in a light rain. Grades run from the easy 5.3 range to 5.12, with most routes between 5.9 and 5.12. Forever Feels Like Home and Pocket Full of Sunshine (5.9) are good moderates, while Hazy Shade of Winter (5.12c) and Circular Semantics are harder tests. It suits repeat laps and quick after-work sessions.
co_ouray_rotary_park_rink_wall.parking_note: Drive about a mile north from central Ouray on US 550 toward Ridgway, turn in at the hockey rink on the right, and park near the public restrooms. The cliff is a few steps away.

co_bookmark_the.blurb: The Bookmark is a granite formation on Lumpy Ridge above Estes Park, between the Bookend and the Book. Nearly every route is trad and most are multi-pitch. Grades concentrate between 5.8 and 5.10, with a handful at 5.11 and 5.12. The granite is technical, with flared cracks, thin protection and a need for careful footwork. Fantasy Ridge (5.9), Romulan Territory (5.10b) and Joy and Tribulation (5.9) are popular, and it is a handy alternative when the Book is crowded. Approaches are mostly flat walking of a mile or more. Afternoon thunderstorms are common, so start early on the longer lines.
co_bookmark_the.parking_note: From Estes Park, go up past the Stanley Hotel, stay on the road as it becomes Devil's Gulch Road, and turn left onto Lumpy Ridge Road about half a mile along. The trailhead lot sits at its end and fills early.
